responsiveness.title: Responsiveness Check
responsiveness.question: Does the person respond when you firmly tap their shoulders and shout?
responsiveness.hint: Firmly tap both shoulders and ask loudly: 'Are you okay? Can you hear me?'

options.label: Yes, they respond or move
options.description: The person talks, groans, blinks, or moves intentionally.

advice.title: Stay With Them & Keep Monitoring
advice.description: The person is responsive. Keep them calm and comfortable while ensuring professional help is en route.
points: Call 112 immediately if they are in pain, confused, or had a sudden collapse.
Do not leave the person unattended.
Help them into a comfortable position (usually sitting or lying down comfortably).
Check their breathing continuously. If they stop responding at any moment, start CPR immediately.

options.label: No, they are completely unresponsive
options.description: No eye opening, no sound, no movement whatsoever.

options.label: Not sure / Weak response
options.description: They are barely reacting, limp, or you cannot tell clearly.

breathing.title: Breathing Check
breathing.question: Are they breathing normally? (Watch chest, listen, and feel)
breathing.hint: Look for normal, rhythmic chest rise. Gasping, snoring, or irregular choking sounds (agonal breathing) is NOT normal breathing.

options.label: Yes, breathing normally and continuously
options.description: Chest rises and falls smoothly and regularly at a normal pace.

advice.title: Place in Recovery Position & Monitor Airway
advice.description: Since they are breathing normally, maintain their airway and watch them closely.
points: Roll them gently onto their side into the Recovery Position so their airway stays clear.
Tilt the chin up slightly to prevent tongue obstruction.
Call 112 if not already done, and report their condition.
Keep checking breathing every 30 seconds. If breathing stops or turns into gasping, start CPR immediately.

options.label: No breath, or only irregular gasping / choking sounds
options.description: Agonal gasps are a sign of cardiac arrest. Compressions are needed immediately.

options.label: Not sure / Cannot feel normal breath
options.description: When in doubt during an emergency, clinical guidelines recommend starting CPR without delay.
